harvest.note: Pry them loose with a flat blade; bent or cracked scales lose their warding.

monsters.name: Young Black Dragon
monsters.blurb: A horse-sized black dragon in its first hunting centuries, glossy, tar-black, reeking of vinegar and rotting reeds; its hide is not yet mail-grade but its organs carry real power.

harvest.note: Too small for mail on their own, but a smith can rivet them onto a shield or cloak lining.
Dangerous: fail by 5+ and the sac ruptures, blasting you with 4d6 acid damage (Dexterity save DC 16 for half).
Drain it into ceramic or glass within the hour; it spoils (and may corrode) in metal flasks.
Draw it from the last breath, where the heat or frost still lingers, and stopper an Essence Vessel within a minute.

monsters.name: Adult Black Dragon
monsters.blurb: A house-sized black tyrant at the height of its strength, whose armour-grade scales and potent heart make it the prize of a lifetime.

harvest.note: Requires a full team and a day of work; a whole adult hide gives at least the 12 intact plates a suit of mail needs.
Dangerous: fail by 5+ and the sac ruptures, blasting you with 8d6 acid damage (Dexterity save DC 19 for half).
Chisel them out at the root; snapping them off halves their value.
Must be cut from the finger-bones in one sheet per wing; a torn membrane is worth a tenth as much.
Reach it through the belly, not the ribcage; it must be removed intact and packed in salt within the hour.
Drain it into ceramic or glass within the hour; it spoils (and may corrode) in metal flasks. Open a neck vein; blood from the body cavity is fouled by the breath glands.
It pools behind the eyes as the dragon dies. Open the vessel close: the essence goes to the nearest warm thing.

monsters.name: Ancient Black Dragon
monsters.blurb: A black dragon older than kingdoms, its glossy, tar-black scales scarred by centuries of war; every scrap of its body is a legendary reagent.

harvest.note: The hide must be flensed in sections with adamantine or dragon-bone blades; ordinary steel dulls within minutes.
Dangerous: fail by 5+ and the sac ruptures, blasting you with 12d6 acid damage (Dexterity save DC 22 for half).
Saw them off at the skull ridge; the base is the most magically dense part.
Pierce the lens and it clouds instantly; must be jarred in preserving salts within the hour.
Reach it through the belly, not the ribcage; it must be removed intact and packed in salt within the hour.
Burst it (fail by 5+) and magical darkness fills a 20-foot radius around you for 10 minutes.
Drain it into ceramic or glass within the hour; it spoils (and may corrode) in metal flasks. Bring a cask's worth of vials; the heart pumps for minutes after death.
Each fang takes an hour to chisel free of the jaw; hurry it and it cracks along the root.
Each wing is the size of a ship's sail: a team needs half a day per wing, and a torn sheet is worth a tenth as much.
It pools behind the eyes as the dragon dies. Open the vessel close: the essence goes to the nearest warm thing.

monsters.name: Ancient Silver Dragon
monsters.blurb: A silver dragon older than most nations, wise and often disguised among mortals; its remains are relics as much as reagents.

harvest.note: The hide must be flensed in sections with adamantine or dragon-bone blades; ordinary steel dulls within minutes.
Dangerous: fail by 5+ and the sac ruptures, blasting you with 12d6 cold damage (Constitution save DC 22 for half).
Dangerous: fail by 5+ and it vents on you — Constitution save against being paralyzed for 1 minute (DC 22).
Pierce the lens and it clouds instantly; must be jarred in preserving salts within the hour.
Reach it through the belly, not the ribcage; it must be removed intact and packed in salt within the hour.
Drain it into ceramic or glass within the hour; it spoils (and may corrode) in metal flasks. Bring a cask's worth of vials; the heart pumps for minutes after death.
Each fang takes an hour to chisel free of the jaw; hurry it and it cracks along the root.
Each wing is the size of a ship's sail: a team needs half a day per wing, and a torn sheet is worth a tenth as much.
Draw it from the last breath, where the heat or frost still lingers, and stopper an Essence Vessel within a minute.

monsters.name: Dragon Turtle
monsters.blurb: An island-sized sea dragon with a spiked shell that capsizes ships and breathes scalding steam; one carcass can outfit a navy.

harvest.note: Plates must be cut free from the carcass in the surf or with it hauled ashore; underwater work takes three times as long.
Dangerous: fail by 5+ and it vents, dealing 8d6 fire damage (Constitution save DC 19 for half) in a 15-foot cloud.
Must be salted within a day or it rots in the sun and loses its water-shedding quality.
Only reachable by cutting through the plastron; a task needing a crew and at least 6 hours.
It pools behind the eyes as the dragon dies. Open the vessel close: the essence goes to the nearest warm thing.

monsters.name: Pseudodragon
monsters.blurb: A cat-sized dragonet with a sleep-venom sting and a telepathic bond with those it favours; most crafters prefer it alive as a familiar.

harvest.note: Prick yourself (fail by 5+) and you must make a DC 11 Constitution save or fall asleep for an hour.
Needs an Essence Vessel within 1 minute of death; if it was someone's familiar, they will feel it go.

monsters.name: Wyvern
monsters.blurb: A two-legged dragon cousin with a lethal tail sting; its venom sac alone can pay for a whole expedition.

harvest.note: Rupture it (fail by 5+) and you take 7d6 poison damage (Constitution save DC 15 for half). Milk it before the carcass cools.
Remove the venom sac first, or the stinger still drips enough to poison you.
One sheet per wing; tears easily if the wyvern crashed from a height.
